name: KRWO
oneLiner: KRWO is a Korean won-pegged stablecoin issued by Gimswap against Open Voucher KRW vouchers at a 10,000:1 ratio; multi-chain ERC-20 with minter privileges.
collateral: Open Voucher (OV) KRW vouchers issued by Open Asset and represented on-chain as OV tokens used as collateral for KRWO issuance
pegMechanism: KRWO is issued against OV tokens at a 10,000 KRWO = 1 OV token/voucher ratio; Open Voucher documentation describes OV vouchers as redeemable for Korean won at 1:1 through the Open Voucher service

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At BSC block 110,070,261 via the public Blast RPC, KRWO.owner() returned 0xc34e0d2b73e5c5a826fa4a86c240cac9fd347c1c, MINTER_ADDRESS() returned GimSwap 0x88cbe5d0088db1dfb302e5c58242153b6171f50b, and a zero-value transfer from an unrelated address succeeded. The exact verified FiatToken source has stock ERC-20 transfer/transferFrom behavior, no blacklist, freeze, pause, seize, or transfer-hook gate, and a minter-only burn(uint256) that burns the minter's own balance; a simulated burn(0) succeeds only from the minter. Its verified GimSwap route burns only KRWO sent into that route before returning OV vouchers, rather than exposing arbitrary holder burn. At Kaia block 221,892,959 via public-en.node.kaia.io, KRWO.owner() returned 0xbe025edc4499c0e50a2c14655ba360a840f47c39, MINTER_ADDRESS() returned 0x663e9d64cdd9b8cc7b0f073bbfb927aa8d154be0, local zero-value transfer and minter-only burn simulations succeeded, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot was zero. Kaiascan does not publish verified source for that deployment, so this review does not encode source absence as direct false. The material backing/redemption route is Open Voucher: GimSwap's verified BSC route points to the upgrade-capable OV contract and the issuer describes OV-to-KRW bank-account refund rails. The issuer's source and documentation describe a 1:1 OV/KRW claim and assert regular reserve audits, but the public site sitemap did not expose issuer terms/legal or a dated proof-of-reserves report. That off-token voucher and redemption dependency remains an upstream access exposure, so inherited is retained rather than suppressing it with a direct no-control finding.
blacklistabilityReview.reviewer: Codex Safety Score V9 access review

mintAuthority.summary: KRWO is a non-upgradeable ERC-20 whose mint() is gated on a single immutable MINTER_ADDRESS on each chain — a GimSwap voucher-swap contract that mints KRWO against Open Voucher (OV) deposits. The owner EOA cannot mint: mint() from the owner reverts UnauthorizedAccount(owner), and setMinter() reverts MinterAlreadySet() for every caller, so the minter is permanently locked and cannot be replaced or added to. The owner retains only transferOwnership/renounceOwnership/setMetadata. Neither the token nor the BSC minter is a proxy; the Kaia minter's owner has been burned to 0x…01, leaving its fee setters unreachable.

controls.label: KRWO minter contract (BSC) — GimSwap voucher swap
controls.capDescription: The token enforces no cap: cap()/maxSupply() are absent from the bytecode and a simulated mint of 1e30 units from this address succeeds. Any bound lives inside the swap contract's voucher accounting.
controls.evidence: At BSC block 109,940,975: MINTER_ADDRESS() on the KRWO token returns 0x88cbe5d0088db1dfb302e5c58242153b6171f50b; eth_getCode returns 4,462 bytes (a contract) and its EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so it is not a proxy. eth_call of mint(0x…dEaD, 1) from this address succeeds, and from every other sender — including the owner EOA — it reverts with UnauthorizedAccount(caller) (custom error 0x32b2baa3). A simulated mint of 1e30 units from this address also succeeds, proving the token applies no cap. The contract exposes TOKEN_CONTRACT()=0x5868a0bc… (KRWO), VOUCHER_CONTRACT()=0x872c7eb7f46ece69c9db74f91ce249c2e1b3c2ea and transferVoucherCallback(address,address,uint256,bytes), i.e. it mints on OV voucher deposit. It has no owner() and no reachable admin setter. Contract source is not verified on BscScan, so its internal voucher accounting is asserted by GimSwap docs rather than read.

controls.label: KRWO minter contract (Klaytn/Kaia) — GimSwap voucher swap
controls.capDescription: The token enforces no cap: cap()/maxSupply() are absent from the bytecode and a simulated mint of 1e30 units from this address succeeds. Any bound lives inside the swap contract's voucher accounting.
controls.evidence: At Klaytn/Kaia block 221,835,246: MINTER_ADDRESS() on the KRWO token returns 0x663e9d64cdd9b8cc7b0f073bbfb927aa8d154be0; eth_getCode returns 6,056 bytes and its EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so it is not a proxy. eth_call of mint(0x…dEaD, 1) and of mint(0x…dEaD, 1e30) from this address both succeed; from any other sender, including the owner EOA, mint() reverts. The contract exposes TOKEN_CONTRACT()=0x7fc69269… (KRWO), VOUCHER_CONTRACT()=0x51ac6833805ac16bc10db649b84128b321b53820 and transferVoucherCallback(...). Its owner() reads 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000000001 — a burn sentinel — so its setFee/resetFeeReceiver/transferOwnership entrypoints are permanently unreachable (feeNumerator() is currently 0 of FEE_DENOMINATOR 10000). Source is not verified on Kaiascan, so internal voucher accounting is asserted by docs rather than read.

controls.label: KRWO owner (BSC) — EOA
controls.evidence: At BSC block 109,940,975: owner() returns 0xc34e0d2b73e5c5a826fa4a86c240cac9fd347c1c and eth_getCode returns 0x (EOA). This EOA has NO mint authority: a simulated mint(0x…dEaD, 1) from it reverts with UnauthorizedAccount(0xc34e0d2b…), and setMinter(address) reverts with MinterAlreadySet() (0xf119708d) for every candidate argument and every caller, so it cannot appoint, replace or add a minter. Its remaining powers are transferOwnership, renounceOwnership and setMetadata(string,string) (token name/symbol). It is also the bonusReceiver() of the BSC minter contract. This corrects the prior record, which listed the owner as a direct-minter.

controls.label: KRWO owner (Klaytn/Kaia) — EOA
controls.evidence: At Klaytn/Kaia block 221,835,246: owner() returns 0xbe025edc4499c0e50a2c14655ba360a840f47c39 and eth_getCode returns 0x (EOA), distinct from the BSC owner. It has NO mint authority: mint() simulated from it reverts, and setMinter(address) reverts for every caller because the minter is already set. Remaining powers are transferOwnership, renounceOwnership and setMetadata. It is the feeReceiver() of the Kaia minter contract. This corrects the prior record, which listed the owner as a direct-minter.

review.evidence: Read at BSC block 109,940,975 and Klaytn/Kaia block 221,835,246. Both KRWO deployments are non-upgradeable: EIP-1967 implementation, admin and beacon slots all read 0x0, and neither runtime bytecode contains upgradeTo(address) or upgradeToAndCall(address,bytes). Contract source is verified on neither BscScan nor Kaiascan (Sourcify has no entry and returned 503 during this review), so authority was established directly on-chain: the full selector set was recovered from the runtime bytecode and resolved against the OpenChain signature database, and each authority claim was then proved by eth_call simulation. The dispatch surface is transfer/transferFrom/approve/allowance/balanceOf/totalSupply/name/symbol/decimals plus mint(address,uint256), burn(uint256), owner(), transferOwnership, renounceOwnership, setMinter(address), setMetadata(string,string), MINTER_ADDRESS(), transferCallback and transferAndCall. There is no cap(), maxSupply(), pause(), blacklist(), grantRole() or configureMinter(). mint() is gated exclusively on MINTER_ADDRESS(): BSC 0x88cbe5d0088db1dfb302e5c58242153b6171f50b, Kaia 0x663e9d64cdd9b8cc7b0f073bbfb927aa8d154be0, both contracts, neither a proxy. Simulated mint from those addresses succeeds (including 1e30 units, so the token applies no cap); simulated mint from any other sender — the owner EOA included — reverts with UnauthorizedAccount(caller). setMinter(address) reverts with MinterAlreadySet() for every caller and every argument, so the minter is permanently locked: no party can replace, add or remove a minter. The owner EOAs (BSC 0xc34e0d2b73e5c5a826fa4a86c240cac9fd347c1c, Kaia 0xbe025edc4499c0e50a2c14655ba360a840f47c39) therefore hold no mint authority at all, only transferOwnership/renounceOwnership/setMetadata. This overturns the previous record, which characterised both owners as direct-minters with unbounded mint ability. Residual limit: because neither minter's source is verified, the voucher-collateral bound enforced inside the swap contract is asserted by GimSwap documentation rather than read; the token-level facts above are all direct on-chain reads.

bridgeRouteRisk.summary: GimSwap docs describe KRWO as issued on Kaia and BNB networks to enable Korean-won transactions. The source evidence supports issuer-native multichain issuance rather than an external bridge route.
